tweets.text:
“Matic” was one of the first ten words my son learned.. and he treats it as the fifth member of the family. 

Using @maticrobots also made it clear to me that useful home robots are here to stay. 

They continue to surprise and delight us with gestures like this - true 10 year overnight success company. 

Kudos to the team!!

(obligatory not an investor, just a fan)

Grok Bot is a fantastic release.. the UX, the design, the onboarding :chefs-kiss:

But I go back and forth on this a lot: Will users (personal and business) want one super agent that holds all the context or sub agents that are designated to do a slice of tasks?

If we treat agents as humans, then the Grok Bot design makes a ton of sense. It allows us to compartmentalize tools, context, outcomes for that person’s division. You reach out to that bot for that specific goal that you have in mind. 

But, if you treat agents as Jarvis, you want a master agent that just gets the job done. It might create and coordinate all the bots (and dare I say the communication/context) that might be needed to do the task. But the interface is 1:1 vs. 1:many. 

My guess is it’ll veer towards the one master agent over time who can then act as an orchestrator who reads / understands the bots you create. But starts narrow as most of the companies are doing it now. 

PS: I understand the core engineering constraints (context windows, tool use, simplicity, cost etc) why companies are choosing task/singular outcomes today. Primarily thinking this from a design / product side.

tweets.text:
Prompt debt is the new tech debt. 

With every model update, you should be cutting at least 50% of your prompts.

Most AI products have bloated prompts that are making your product quality worse.

The typical flow is: model fails at something -> add 10 rules. Tool call fails -> add 10 examples. Output is weird -> add formatting constraints.

3 months later, your system prompt is a novel. 

Meanwhile the model is way smarter and your micro-managey prompts are turning it into a dumb rules machine.

I miss when teams actually whiteboarded. Sad casualty of the Covid wfh era.

There was something playful about standing around a board, drawing half-baked ideas, interrupting each other and jointly shaping things.

Years of Zoom and Google Meet seem to have beaten that instinct out of people.

tweets.text:
Awesome day in terms of new model releases from both Deepseek and Grok. Both of these new model updates represent huge jumps in capability at insanely low costs. 

This is truly Jevons paradox for AI playing out. By bringing down the cost of AI, demand will continue to accelerate. When I talk to enterprises, they have vastly more use-cases for what they’d like agents to handle than generally what they’re able to budget for today. 

They want agents to scan their codebases for security issues. They want agents to review all their documents. They want agents to process information in a large portion of their workflows. And so on. When we bring down the cost of AI or drive up capability levels, it opens up all new use cases in the enterprises, which drives even greater demand.

This is also great for the applied AI layer. The more choice of models - especially those tuned for different types (or costs) of work - the more value there is in being at the layer that can route and optimize based on the task. Great for the entire stack right now.

tweets.text:
韩国监管机构这两天出了一个极其离谱的新规：

从 8 月 19 日起，所有新投资者必须通过为期 5 天（累计满 5 小时）的模拟交易测试，才被允许购买单股杠杆 ETF🤡。

这个规定目前在一部分投资社区里被无情的调侃为，“你现在必须向政府证明自己不是大傻子，才配去杠杆市场里送钱。”

为了按住大家的手，韩国政府这次把准入门槛直接拉到了“防沉迷”的级别：

新股民不仅要在模拟盘里枯坐满 5 个小时，还要通过 3 个小时的强制在线培训，甚至账户里的最低现金存款必须达到 3000 万韩元（约 2.1 万美元）。

而之所以监管急成这样，自然是韩国散户之前在那波存储暴跌中损失惨重，以及杠杆ETF加剧了波动。

不过，一边是苦口婆心为你好，想必另一边必然有“不要你管，我能东山再起”的抵触情绪。

投资修罗场，修炼技术也修心。

土狗 meme 币的营销，现在已经狂到敢直接跑到法庭直播现场蹦迪了。

目前，美国一起备受全美关注的“Clancy 杀婴惨案”正式开庭，因为案情极其沉重且社会影响巨大，Court TV 和福克斯新闻决定全网开庭审直播。

结果，评论区瞬间涌现大量垃圾 Bots 疯狂复读一个词叫“grokvantage”。

刚开始，看直播的普通网友全被搞懵了，怀疑是不是马斯克的 xAI 搞出了什么 grok 相关的产品；

结果懂行的 reddit 网友们进去一扒，底裤直接露出来了：
跟 AI 半毛钱关系没有，单纯就是某个土狗币蹭 Grok 概念准备搞发射，来评论区刷 Bot 来营销一波。

在法庭庭审评论区搞这事，真不怕搞出大舆情，最后反向顺着网线把 Dev（项目方开发者）给抓进去吗？

很多网友应该都发现了，现在闭源巨头们为了抢夺训练 AI 的“数据资产”，已经开始不择手段了。

前有 Anthropic 焚书训练，现有亚马逊白嫖用户视频。

亚马逊最近给旗下的直播平台 Twitch （俗称老鼠台）出了一个极其阴损的绝招：

直接白嫖用户的直播和回放来训练自家 AI，并且故意把拒绝选项藏到了几乎找不着的地方。

你得先进入“设置”，点击“隐私与安全”（Privacy and Security），然后一路往下滑到最底部，才能在一个极其不起眼的卡片里找到“数据授权”选项。

他们故意把拒绝（Opt-out）按钮的字号缩得极小，甚至还用了一堆绕口的法务黑话来模糊概念，就是打赌大部分普通人根本没有耐心翻到这一页。

有没有国内摇一摇开屏广告的味道了？无法拒绝，防不胜防。

更有意思的是，如果你是欧洲（EU）的用户，因为有硬核的 GDPR 法案撑腰，Twitch 甚至连这个开关都不敢给你上，直接在底层就默认不抓取。

但对于美国和全球其他地区的普通主播和用户，那就是能割一茬是一茬，默认所有人全部同意。

tweets.text:
Everyone has a different trading style, and not everyones trading style works well with person to person. 

I typically have two trades I take and I stick to them. Those trades are also heavily context dependent. For example, not really having traded crypto for the past year. Just like staying out in prev bear markets is bc of the context/macro trends. 

One is a defensive trade, other is reclaim at what I call historical supports. But the reclaim itself isnt as important to me as is the history of the spot. The defensive trade is at a htf spot with a sharp sell off that isn't looking for a trend reversal but a lower high. While the reclaim is typically an end to end trade. 

Core postions are a bit different in the fact that something i have conviction in. The core doesnt get touched, but I will trade around the core on a different brokerage in order to. Llower the effective cost average, or accumulate more shares. The core itself is a longer term belief where as 90% of what I trade means nothing to me at all. So there are both low time frame, and high time frames trades and beliefs. 

I will post some examples of the actual style with context. But again there are some things you just cant really describe. Like gut. There's a lot of thoughts and feelings that go into buying and selling that you can't put on paper.

There is so much more access to gambling on anything and everything these days where as crypto use to be the easiest outlet. 

Sports gambling, online casinos, prediction markets, trading cards, easier access to equities and soon easier access to private markets. All of this has actually taken away from crypto on top of the AI boom bc people have more choices. Not everyone wants to gamble on chain. There is now something for everyone, with ease of access. That has fractured some liquidity in this market

Things I think about for my overall portfolio is having both a wealth creation aspect, and a wealth preservation aspect.  having a set target for overall volatility.  Having orthogonal and convex bets. Smoothing the path of returns which has been a god send.  Having my trading fees be zero Trying to use limit orders vs crossing the spread as often as possible. using tax aware strategies. Whether that be something like AQR to offset ordinary income, or PPLI to have tax free growth where you can wrap your assets inside for high turnover strategies allowing you to compound tax free. These all make a complete book and allow for max growth.

tweets.text:
Not a great month for hardware wallets.

Trezor disclosed a breach at its shipping provider affecting ~13.7K recent customers. ~11.7K had full name, email, phone and shipping address exposed. Trezor systems/private keys were not compromised. The leak directly links identities and physical addresses to known crypto holders, creating significant phishing, social-engineering and potential physical-security risk.

Hardware wallets are often considered "more secure" than software wallets. While I still think that is "generally true" in a few specific aspects, this incident reinforces an advantage of software self-custody wallets (such as Binance Web3 Wallet & Trust Wallet), without purchasing and shipping a physical device that links a user's identity and address to crypto ownership.

Not saying hardware wallets are "bad". Just different risk profiles. YZiLabs is an investor in many hardware wallets.

Security, privacy and convenience comes in many different shapes. The more we can educate our communities, the better.

tweets.text: the FIRE token leans lower after its operator paid 11 wallets a total of 0.0231 GME Stock Tokens. when traders trade less, FIRE buys fewer rewards, so holders get less for keeping a streak that tops out at 90 days and resets on a sale. the protocol can replace GME anyway.

the SEC pushes issuer-linked tokens lower near term after canceling its August 14 crypto offering vote with no replacement date. with the rule at OIRA for 146 days against the usual 90, issuers still lack public terms for a U.S. fundraising route.

with KPMG signing off, Tether leans higher in private markets. prospective investors held up a raise of up to $20b over financial transparency. after auditing token liabilities, cash flows and assets, KPMG gave an unqualified opinion on 2025 accounts showing a $6.814b surplus.
